statement_en: Let $\mu$ be a $\sigma$-finite measure on $X$. For functions $$f_n(x)\in L^p(X\to \mathbb{C},\mu),\quad 1\leq p\leq \infty,$$ there exists an $f\in L^p$ such that $\|f_n-f\|_{L^p}\to 0$ if and only if for every $\varepsilon>0$ there exists a positive integer $N_{\varepsilon}$ such that for all $n,m>N_{\varepsilon}$, $$\|f_n-f_m\|_{L^p}<\varepsilon.$$
key_techniques: Cauchy criterion in a normed space
callout_body: $\mu$是装备在$X$上的$\sigma-$finite的测度。函数列$$f_n(x)\in L^p(X\to \mathbb{C},\mu),\infty\geq p\geq 1$$的极限存在,即存在一个$f \in L^p$使得$||f_n-f||_{L^p}\to 0$，当且仅当$\forall \varepsilon>0$存在正整数$N_{\varepsilon}$使得任意$n,m>N_{\varepsilon}$都有$$||f_n-f_m||_{L^p}<\varepsilon$$
